expectations.text: Pushes back on the 'are you sure?' modal as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: modal is the weakest device on the ladder for this problem; Generic 'Are you sure?' modal — bottom of the list

expectations.text: Explains habituation or click-through blindness as why frequent dialogs stop working
expectations.evidence: users will click through 'Are you sure?' on reflex — same muscle memory as dismissing a cookie banner

expectations.text: Recommends reversibility (soft delete with a retention window) as the strongest option
expectations.evidence: Make it reversible — soft-delete with a retention window (e.g. 30 days), listed as #1 in preference order

expectations.text: Recommends grace-period undo as a strong low-friction option
expectations.evidence: Grace-period undo — delete immediately, show 'Workspace deleted. Undo' for ~10s, listed as #2

expectations.text: Recommends type-the-workspace-name confirmation for the irreversible case
expectations.evidence: Type-to-confirm — typing the workspace name, for genuinely high-blast-radius/irreversible cases

expectations.text: If a dialog is retained, requires it to name the workspace and the scale of what is lost
expectations.evidence: it needs to name the specific thing ('Delete workspace 'Acme Corp' and its 14 members?')

expectations.text: Notes that the server must enforce the deletion rules, not just the UI
expectations.evidence: No mention of server-side enforcement principle; discusses backend as implementation detail but not as enforcement authority

expectations.text: Gives an explicit preference order rather than an undifferentiated list of ideas
expectations.evidence: Preference order for destructive actions (strongest first): 1. Make it reversible 2. Grace-period undo 3. Type-to-confirm 4. Generic modal
